_meta.description: Cumulative ad creative learnings from StoreHub Q3–Q4 2025 performance data across MY, PH, TH. Visual design patterns added 2026-03-17 from full creative library review.

headline_insights.rule: Question hooks ('How much are you paying in delivery fees?', 'How much is your profit?') deliver the lowest CPL in PH — RM41 vs RM99 avg
headline_insights.evidence: PH Q4: howmuchisyourprofit_coffee CPL RM41, howmuchisyourprofit_halohalo CPL RM37

headline_insights.rule: Price anchor headlines (e.g., '55% Off', 'PHP63/month') drive both volume and quality when paired with hardware visual
headline_insights.evidence: MY Q4: 55% Promo V2 SQL% 33.5%; PH: PHP63 is the top-performing PH message across 2 quarters

headline_insights.rule: Transformation narratives ('Stress to Success') fail as acquisition hooks — 0 SQLs across 5 PH variants
headline_insights.evidence: PH Q3+Q4: StressToSuccess all variants, all zero SQLs. Retired.

headline_insights.rule: #1 POS System + promo outperforms #1 POS + logos as supporting point in PH
English language in MY drives highest Win% (close rates); Chinese drives highest SQL%; Malay drives volume
headline_insights.evidence: MY Q3 final takeaway + Q3 individual ad performance

visual_insights.rule: Choose Your Fighter (side-by-side hardware comparison) is a cross-market winner — CTR 3.95% in MY, 4.86% in PH, both 4x+ market benchmark
visual_insights.evidence: MY Q4: Falcon CYF CTR 3.95%, D3 CYF CPL RM47 CPWon RM721; PH Q4: Falcon CYF CTR 4.86% SQL% 38.3%

visual_insights.rule: Split-screen format (product visual + offer text) consistently outperforms full-frame product or full-frame text in MY
visual_insights.evidence: MY Q3 final: 'Split-screen + Promo creatives consistently perform best'; BAU D3 Mini Split Screen CPL RM116

visual_insights.rule: Stop-motion unboxing video is the highest-volume PH format — CPL RM48 at RM37k spend
Blooper/unexpected opening hook in TH drives 2-3x video engagement vs standard openings — Hook Rate 0.50% vs 0.15% avg
visual_insights.note: No wins yet in TH — engagement signal only, not proven bottom-funnel

visual_insights.rule: Generic product-only white background ads have near-zero conversion — confirmed multiple markets
visual_insights.evidence: MY Q4: White Background 0 leads; D3 White Background CPL RM212 SQL% low

visual_insights.rule: Comic/illustrated promo format achieves lowest CPWon in MY Q3 (RM707) — visual differentiation works
visual_insights.evidence: MY Q3: EN_Comic Promo_KL CPWon RM707

visual_insights.rule: F&B vertical-specific imagery (restaurant setting, F&B hardware context) lifts SQL% vs generic — PH Allinonepos_Fnb SQL% 45% vs generic 20-25%

offer_insights.rule: BAU evergreen price promo is the most scalable ad type — RM62,988 MY spend at CPL RM64
offer_insights.evidence: MY Q4: BAU Promo — highest spend, CPL RM64 (47% below benchmark)

offer_insights.rule: Percentage discounts (55% off) paired with hardware convert better than flat price alone in MY
offer_insights.evidence: MY Q4: 55% Promo V2 SQL% 33.5%, CPWon RM1,415

offer_insights.rule: High absolute price as primary hook (₱21,000) creates CPL spike — 4.6x benchmark — even if SQL% is high
Seasonal hooks (Raya, Merdeka, Independence Day) boost performance when paired with price — not effective alone
offer_insights.evidence: MY Q3: EN_Merdeka Promo CPWon RM885 (best Q3); PH Q3: Independence Day P63 = SQL% 43%

audience_insights.rule: F&B-specific vertical targeting in copy/visuals improves SQL% by ~2x vs generic in PH
audience_insights.evidence: PH Q4: Allinonepos_Fnb SQL% 45% vs Allinonepos generic SQL% ~20%

audience_insights.rule: Retail vertical is critically undertested in MY and PH — only handful of retail-specific ads, none at scale
audience_insights.evidence: MY Q4: Retail Business Types series all <RM1k spend; PH: no retail-specific ads
audience_insights.action: Create dedicated retail vertical test batch

format_insights.rule: Video generally outperforms static for CTR and engagement — but static can match or beat video on SQL% when offer is crystal clear
format_insights.evidence: PH Q3: Static Allinonepos CPWon RM693; PH Q4: static outperforms some video on SQL%

format_insights.rule: Multi-element openings (AI + comparison + speech stacked) kill performance — single clear hook required
format_insights.evidence: MY Q3: EN_Choose Your Fighter + AI Intro + Speech = 0 wins at RM9,684

visual_design_patterns._note: Observed from full creative library review 2026-03-17. These are actual design executions and their characteristics.

proven_layouts.name: Choose Your Fighter — Diagonal Split
proven_layouts.description: Diagonal dividing line splits frame into two contrasting halves (blue left / orange right). Each half has one hardware product with playful label. VS badge in center. Bold dark pill headline across top.
key_elements: no body copy — visual tells the story
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Game/fighting game reference creates instant engagement. Comparison frame answers 'which one for me?' which merchants actively want to know.

proven_layouts.name: Split Card — Product + Feature List
proven_layouts.description: Frame divided into two rounded-corner cards side by side. Left: hardware on brand-color pedestal/BG. Right: feature list or comparison on accent color (pink/coral). Bottom strip: social proof + CTA.
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Clear information hierarchy. Product proof left, benefit proof right. Social proof lands after desire is created.

proven_layouts.name: Bold Text Overlay on Moody Photography
proven_layouts.description: Dark/moody restaurant or store environment photo as full-bleed background. White bold headline (Barlow Black) dominates center-left. Feature list below in smaller text. Orange corner banner for claim (#1 POS, BIR Accredited etc). Logo bottom.
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Aspirational setting. The merchant sees their own restaurant. Premium feel.

proven_layouts.name: Illustrated Problem — Soft Background
proven_layouts.description: Warm cream/off-white background. Central illustration of problematic scenario (loading POS, error screen). Relatable copy below in two sizes. CTA in brand orange. Logo bottom.
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Breaks from photography-heavy feed. Cartoon reduces threat of 'this is an ad'. Problem is universally understood instantly.

proven_layouts.name: Price Anchor Comparison (Bundle vs Individual)
proven_layouts.description: 50/50 split. Left: individual pricing stacked with crossed-out prices/money emoji. Right: bundle at fraction of price with checklist. Bottom: hardware visual + '#1 POS' claim + daily price breakdown.
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Price shock via contrast. ₱9,621 vs ₱2,499 triggers loss aversion. Daily breakdown (₱75/day) makes it feel trivial.

proven_layouts.name: Before/After Emotional Split
proven_layouts.description: Left half: stressed merchant with old/broken POS (green CRT, error screen, dark moody). Right half: happy merchant with StoreHub (bright, clean). Strong contrasting emotion headline at top.
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Emotional contrast tells the whole story in 1 second. Aspirational identity — merchants want to be the right-side merchant.

proven_layouts.name: Word Repetition / Text Pattern Burst
proven_layouts.description: Discount or key message repeated 8-10 times in a diagonal grid as background texture. Hardware breaks through/overlaps the text. Minimal other copy.
key_elements: hardware cutout breaks out of grid
seen_in: Up to PHP 20,000 OFF repeated pattern
proven_layouts.why_it_works: High visual energy. The repetition burns the price into the viewer. Stops scroll because it looks different.

proven_layouts.name: Cultural Hook + Local Food Hero
proven_layouts.description: Large local food photograph dominates frame (halo-halo, nasi lemak etc). 2-3 lines of native-language text in large bold font bottom-left. Logo top-right, minimal. NO product visible.
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Stops the scroll because it looks like food content, not an ad. Native language + local food = immediate cultural resonance. Curiosity gap created by question.
proven_layouts.notes: This format is UNDERUSED — only one execution seen. Very high potential for MY (Bahasa + nasi lemak/roti canai) and TH.

proven_layouts.name: Aspirational Lifestyle — Merchant as Hero
proven_layouts.description: Merchant (wearing apron) in aspirational, ethereal setting (floating on clouds, running in flower field). Feature tags/pills float around them. Headline: 'What running your business feels like with StoreHub'. Offer badge at bottom.
seen_in: What running your business feels like — illustrated
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Sells the feeling, not the features. Merchants are sold on vision of less stress/more freedom. Rare in this library — differentiator.
proven_layouts.notes: Photo variant (real merchant in field) likely stronger than illustrated. Test both.

proven_layouts.name: Google Reviews Ranking Comparison
proven_layouts.description: Dark charcoal background. Question headline. Ranked list of competitors below with star ratings and review counts. StoreHub highlighted/elevated vs weaker competitors.
seen_in: StoreHub ranks #1 — 4.7 stars / 2,533 reviews vs Qashier, Zeoniq, FeedMe
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Third-party social proof. The merchant already trusts Google Reviews. Seeing competitors with 5, 66, 160 reviews vs 2,533 is immediately decisive.
proven_layouts.notes: UNDERUSED. Only one execution. High potential for MY (Qashier/Zeoniq awareness) and PH.

proven_layouts.name: Seasonal AI Scene Context
proven_layouts.description: Hardware placed on a counter in an AI-generated seasonal scene (Christmas decorations, Halloween pumpkins, CNY lanterns/dragons). Feature bubbles/pills float around device. Offer badge. Logo bottom.
proven_layouts.why_it_works: Timely. Matches the feed context the merchant is already seeing. Novelty of seasonal scene triggers curiosity.

typography_in_use.hero_headlines: Barlow Black / ExtraBold — all caps or title case, very large (fills 30-50% of frame width)
typography_in_use.sub_headlines: Barlow Bold or Open Sans Bold
typography_in_use.playful_labels: Rounded/bubbly fonts seen in CYF labels and CNY ads — likely Nunito or similar
typography_in_use.price_display: Very large, bold, often colored (orange or white) — price is treated as a visual element not just copy

color_usage_patterns.primary_bg: Brand orange (#ff9419) used as dominant BG in ~30% of ads
color_usage_patterns.cream_bg: Off-white/cream (#f5e8d8 approx) used for soft illustrated ads
color_usage_patterns.accent_pink_coral: Used as secondary card BG in split layouts — seen in PH ads
color_usage_patterns.accent_blue: #2a6ee8 used sparingly — CTA buttons in some PH ads
color_usage_patterns.seasonal_override: CNY = red + gold. Halloween = purple + orange. Christmas = red + green (but always orange CTA)

cta_button_styles_observed: Full-width orange pill button — most common
Orange text with arrow '→' — no button, just styled text (Loyalty cascade ad)
White pill with dark text — occasional
badge_styles_observed: Orange diagonal corner ribbon — '#1 POS System in Philippines'
Circular seal — BIR Accredited (PH compliance trust signal)
Blue pill/badge — '#1 POS System in MY'
Announcement megaphone icon with price — common in PH 'as low as' ads

untested_visual_concepts: Real merchant face in store environment (candid/documentary style) — only AI-generated or stock used so far
Sequential storytelling within a single static frame (comic strip, morning → evening)
Minimal text / single word headline (e.g., just 'FINALLY.' on full-bleed image)
Overhead aerial shot of food/product (inventory chaos overhead was compelling — apply to F&B)
Malay-language static with local food hero (Bahasa + rendang/nasi lemak visual)
Thai-language cultural hook with Thai food visual
Competitor logo with red X vs StoreHub with green tick (more explicit than current FiatQCV1 approach)
WhatsApp/SMS notification screenshot style — merchant receiving win-back customer message
Real Google/FB review screenshot as ad visual (authentic social proof format)

hardware_photos.notes: Use market-specific hardware shots — MY hardware vs PH hardware differ visually (branding/color)

ui_icons.line_icons: line-icons_* series — POS features, delivery, loyalty, analytics etc
ui_icons.orange_icons: Orange-icons_* series — colored product feature icons

illustrations.notes: Rich illustration library. Local food icons are UNDERUSED in ads — huge potential for culturally-native creatives

negative_learnings.rule: NEVER run generic testimonial ads as acquisition creative — confirmed failure across MY and PH
negative_learnings.nuance: This applied to previous low-quality testimonial executions. The 2026 testimonial creative system (real merchant faces + specific outcome quotes + vertical branding) is a fundamentally different product and has NOT been tested at scale. The 'NEVER' applies to logo walls and generic 'I love StoreHub' quotes — not to outcome-specific merchant stories with real faces.

negative_learnings.rule: NEVER run plain unboxing without offer/CTA — scalable spend but low SQL% and very high CPWon
negative_learnings.evidence: MY Q3: CN_D3 Mini Unboxing CPWon RM15,667

negative_learnings.rule: NEVER run Stress-to-Success creative angle in PH — 5 variants, 0 SQLs
NEVER stack multiple competing hooks (AI + product + comparison) — creates confusion and kills conversion
NEVER use price as sole hook without product/hardware visual — drives high CPL
NEVER use dark backgrounds in static ads — confirmed lower performance
negative_learnings.evidence: Implicit from MY analysis + brand guideline note

winning_patterns.name: The MY Champion Formula
winning_patterns.description: Hardware visual + split-screen + % price discount + evergreen or seasonal hook

winning_patterns.name: The PH Champion Formula
winning_patterns.description: All-In-One POS + F&B vertical specificity + specific price anchor (PHP63) + hardware visual
winning_patterns.format: Stop-motion video or clean static with bold headline

winning_patterns.name: Choose Your Fighter Universal
winning_patterns.description: Side-by-side hardware tier comparison — works cross-market, high CTR, strong SQL%
winning_patterns.notes: Works best with Falcon hardware (premium tier creates aspiration)

winning_patterns.name: Question Hook - Profit/Cost
winning_patterns.description: Open with a direct question about the merchant's current cost pain. Drives highest-intent clicks.
winning_patterns.example: How much is your profit? / How much are you paying in delivery fees?

champion_ads.metric: Scale — CPL RM64 at RM63k spend
SQL% 45%, CPWon RM630 — best in dataset
Highest video engagement in TH (Hook Rate 0.50%)
